idiom_name: gRPC C++ generated Service interface + NewStub(channel) with protobuf messages
implementation_notes: The remote interface and the transfer objects come from protoc: the gRPC C++ plugin generates a service class holding a stub for clients, an abstract Service interface for the server and protobuf message classes as payloads. The facade is the class implementing ::Service - its methods take the request and response protobufs and return a grpc::Status - and the client builds a grpc::Channel and calls NewStub. Channel plumbing, HTTP/2 framing, deadlines and serialisation replace the hand-written proxy, so only the coarse delegation and the mapping remain. The classic form (a hand-written facade class plus a client proxy over a protocol of your own) is still justified when the binaries cannot take the protobuf/gRPC dependency or must speak an existing proprietary protocol.
pitfalls: Service methods are invoked concurrently, so shared mutable state in the facade must be synchronised or made immutable.
A grpc::ClientContext belongs to exactly one call; reusing it for a second RPC is undefined behaviour.
A coarse response that would exceed the maximum message size must be turned into a streaming RPC rather than into one giant message.

variants.name: Hand-written facade class and client proxy over a custom framing
variants.idiom_name: hand-written coarse facade class + transfer-object structs + client-side proxy class
variants.implementation_notes: Without an RPC framework the pattern is exactly the classic structure: a facade class with one coarse method per use case, flat transfer-object structs, and a client-side proxy class that serialises the request, writes it to the transport and waits for the reply; explicit framing, deadlines and an error or status type carry what a framework would otherwise generate. Choose it when the wire protocol is fixed by an existing peer or when the generated-code/runtime footprint of gRPC or Thrift is unacceptable, and be prepared to own compatibility on both sides.
pitfalls: With no IDL the proxy and the facade drift silently; every signature change has to be versioned on both sides by hand.
The framing must be length-delimited and every reply correlated to its request, otherwise a partial read or a stale reply corrupts the call.
